findings.body:
**Protect unpushed branch commits when no worktree remains.**

The unpushed-work checks only inspect listed worktrees. After `removePrWorktree` removes a clean checkout containing an unpushed commit, the review branch still retains that commit. On the next resolution, no candidate reaches either check. Line 689 then uses `-B`, which force-resets the existing branch to `expectedSha`. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/v2.47.0/builtin/worktree.c))

This removes the branch reference to the unpushed work. Before resetting an existing `reviewBranch`, check its commits against `expectedSha`, even when no worktree holds it. Refuse or preserve a durable reference when commits would be discarded.
findings.title: Protect unpushed branch commits when no worktree remains.

findings.body:
**Check ignored files before removing a checkout.**

A stale checkout can contain an ignored, unowned file while its tracked files are clean and its HEAD passes the unpushed-work guard. Non-forced `git worktree remove` does not protect ignored files; Git checks status without ignored files, then deletes the directory recursively. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/v2.31.0/builtin/worktree.c))

At `src/adapters/git/prWorktree.ts:644`, removal can therefore delete local content without invoking `onStaleRefresh`. Line 782 has the same gap. Add an ignored/untracked ownership check before both removal paths. Refuse removal when unowned content remains.






Also applies to: 782-782
findings.title: Check ignored files before removing a checkout.

findings.body:
**Block ambient graft files from rewriting commit history.**

At `src/adapters/git/ratchetGit.ts:91`, `GIT_GRAFT_FILE` survives the environment scrub. With real history `A -> B -> C`, a graft that assigns `A` as C's parent makes `gitRangeCommits(A, C)` omit B.

Git 2.39 loads grafts independently of `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS`. Pin `GIT_GRAFT_FILE` to `devNull` so graph reads cannot use substituted parents. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/git/git/v2.39.0/environment.c))
findings.title: Block ambient graft files from rewriting commit history.

findings.body:
**Pass `--no-follow-tags` to the leased push.**

`GIT_HARDEN` does not pin `push.followTags`, and `gitPushAtomic` does not pass `--no-follow-tags`. When `push.followTags=true` is set in the user's Git configuration, `push` also sends missing annotated tags reachable from the pushed branch. These tags are not in `updates`, so they have no lease and are not in the validated set. `--atomic` includes them in the same transaction. The sibling push in `mergeEffects.ts` already passes `--no-follow-tags` for this reason.

```diff
 const res = await execGitWithEnv(
   repo,
   [
     'push',
     '--atomic',
     '--porcelain',
     '--no-verify',
+    '--no-follow-tags',
     ...leases,
     '--end-of-options',
     url,
     ...updates.map((u) => u.refspec),
   ],
   env,
 );
```
findings.title: Pass `--no-follow-tags` to the leased push.

findings.body:
**Stop merge evaluation from running configured merge drivers.**

`gitMergeTreeClean` runs `merge-tree --write-tree` without any option that disables merge drivers. When both parents change the same regular file differently, Git's ort merge calls `ll_merge`. If the file's attribute selects `merge=probe` and `merge.probe.driver` is set, Git runs that configured program. The `.gitattributes` entry can come from the merged tree, but the driver command must come from configuration. The module's threat model treats repository config as possibly untrusted on self-hosted or local runs. `GIT_HARDEN` pins `core.fsmonitor=false` because a configured program would otherwise run. It has no equivalent for merge drivers. Isolate merge evaluation from repository and global configuration before invoking Git.
findings.title: Stop merge evaluation from running configured merge drivers.
